assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Formulation
items.clue: A mixture that has been designed as a useful product.

items.label: Rf value
items.clue: Distance moved by the substance divided by distance moved by the solvent.

items.label: Boiling point
items.clue: The specific temperature at which a pure element or compound changes from liquid to gas.

items.label: Melting point
items.clue: The specific temperature at which a pure element or compound changes from solid to liquid.

questions.stem: Which of these is the definition of a formulation?

options.text: Any mixture containing two or more substances
A compound made by mixing elements together
A mixture designed as a useful product
A pure substance made to an exact recipe

questions.explanation: This is the specification's definition: a formulation is a mixture that has been designed as a useful product.

questions.stem: In paper chromatography, which phase is stationary and which is mobile?

options.text: Solvent stationary, the dyes are mobile
Paper stationary, solvent mobile
Paper stationary, the ink is mobile
Solvent stationary, the paper mobile

questions.explanation: The paper never moves and the solvent rises through it, so the paper is stationary and the solvent mobile.

questions.stem: Why are the components of a formulation mixed in carefully measured quantities?

options.text: So the mixture becomes one pure compound as it is stirred
So the components all react and leave no waste behind
So the product has exactly the properties it was designed to have
They need not be measured; only the ingredients matter

questions.explanation: The quantities are part of the design, and the proportions are what give the product its required properties.

questions.stem: Why do the substances in a mixture end up at different heights on a chromatogram?

options.text: Heavier substances are pulled back down the paper by gravity
The smallest particles fit through the gaps in the paper first
Each substance dissolves in a different part of the solvent
They are distributed differently between the paper and the solvent

questions.explanation: Separation depends on the distribution of substances between the stationary and mobile phases.

questions.stem: A student is given information about four substances. Which one is a formulation?

options.text: A paint with pigment, binder and solvent in fixed amounts
Sea water, a mixture of water and many different dissolved salts
Distilled water sold in bottles for topping up an iron
Nitrogen taken from air and used to fill food packets

questions.explanation: Components with particular purposes, mixed in measured quantities to make a useful product, define a formulation.

questions.stem: What does the Rf value of a compound compare?

options.text: The distance the spot moved up the paper, in centimetres
How far the compound moved against how far the solvent moved
How far the spot moved against the length of the paper
How far the solvent moved against how far the compound spot went

questions.explanation: Rf is the ratio of the distance moved by the compound to the distance moved by the solvent.

questions.stem: A jeweller melts 75% gold with measured amounts of copper and silver to make a harder gold alloy. Is the alloy a formulation?

options.text: No, because a formulation has to be a liquid such as a paint
No, because metals are elements, so alloys are pure
No, the metals join into a single pure metal
Yes: measured amounts are mixed to give a useful product

questions.explanation: Components in carefully measured quantities give the required property, hardness, so this is a formulation.

questions.stem: Which equation gives the Rf value of a substance?

options.text: Rf = distance moved by substance x distance moved up by solvent
Rf = distance moved by substance / total length of paper
Rf = distance moved by substance / distance moved by solvent
Rf = distance moved by the solvent / distance moved by substance

questions.explanation: This is the equation exactly as the specification gives it.

questions.stem: A sample is run in three different solvents and gives one spot each time. What does this show?

options.text: The sample is a pure compound
The sample must be a single element
The spots have simply overlapped
Its Rf is the same in all three solvents

questions.explanation: A pure compound produces a single spot in all solvents, which is what has been found here.

questions.stem: Two dyes give the same Rf value in one solvent. What should the student do next?

options.text: Run them again in a different solvent and compare
Repeat the run in the same solvent for longer
Conclude that the dyes are the same compound
Decide that both of the dyes must be pure

questions.explanation: Different compounds usually have different Rf values in a different solvent, so this tests the match.

questions.stem: A dye is held strongly by the paper and dissolves only slightly in the solvent. On the chromatogram this dye will

options.text: travel with the solvent front, as dissolved dyes do
stay on the line, unable to enter the paper
move furthest of all, being the lightest one
move only a short way up, giving a low Rf value

questions.explanation: Strong attraction to the stationary phase keeps the dye near the origin, so its Rf value is small.

questions.stem: A chromatogram is run on a food colouring. Which result shows that the colouring is impure?

options.text: It gives a single spot, proving it is pure
The colouring separates into more than one spot
Its spot is bigger than the spot of the reference dye
Its Rf value differs from the reference dye's value

questions.explanation: The compounds in a mixture separate into different spots, so several spots show the sample is impure.
